summary: This is a sophisticated phishing email impersonating Australia Post. It falsely claims there are 'overdue accounts' requiring your attention and directs you to click links or reply with personal information. Legitimate Australia Post communications do not mention overdue accounts or ask you to verify details via email — they use your official tracking portal or SMS.
redFlags: Impersonation of Australia Post with fake case reference numbers
False claim about 'overdue accounts' — a common phishing pressure tactic
Mismatched sender: email comes from a redacted address, not an official Australia Post domain (@auspost.com.au)
Suspicious contact info: [NAME] listed as contact with non-official phone and website (example-unrelated-site.com.au — not Australia Post)
Generic greeting '[NAME]' and generic responder 'Anthony A' — unprofessional for official Australia Post
Multiple email redirects requesting replies — classic phishing pattern to harvest responses
Embedded mailto: links designed to capture replies with sensitive information
Login portal link (auspost.com.au/portal) — could be spoofed or lead to credential harvesting
Redacted personal information (TFN, Medicare number, phone, email, name) suggests this is a mass phishing campaign adapted to each victim
Poor grammar: 'regarding to some overdue accounts' and 'regarding to this enquiry' — non-native English phrasing
nextSteps: DO NOT click any links in this email or reply to it
DO NOT provide any personal or banking information
Verify directly with Australia Post: Go to auspost.com.au or call 13 POST (13 7678) using a phone number you find independently
If you have genuine parcels pending, log into your own Australia Post account (not via a link in this email) to check status
Report this phishing attempt to Scamwatch at scamwatch.gov.au
If you have clicked links or shared information, contact IDCARE on 1800 595 160 for identity protection advice
